 K-Wellness Skin Strategy: Pani Bottle Packs Sunscreen to Help Prevent UV-Related Skin Aging and Cancer 
 by Kim Bo Mi

 by Shin You Bin 
 Updated 2026/11/03 13:00 
 Celebrity Health
UV exposure increases the risk of skin aging and skin cancer
Sunscreen with SPF 30 or higher is essential even on cloudy days
--> 
 Travel YouTubers Pani Bottle, 39 years old, and producer Na Young-seok, 50 years old, recently prepared to leave for Matsuyama, Japan, with only the minimum amount of luggage on the YouTube channel ‘Channel Sipoya.’ /Photo=Screenshot from the YouTube channel ‘Channel Sipoya’ 
 Because ultraviolet radiation affects the skin regardless of the season or weather, it is important to make a habit of consistently protecting the skin.
Travel YouTuber Pani Bottle, 39 years old, and producer Na Young-seok, 50 years old, recently prepared to leave for Matsuyama, Japan, with only the minimum amount of luggage on the YouTube channel ‘Channel Sipoya.’ Pani Bottle sorted out the items he needed, including his passport, camera and charger, and packed sunscreen, saying, “When filming, the one thing I always ask to be guaranteed is sunscreen.”
 ◇Ultraviolet radiation penetrates deep into the skin and accelerates aging
 Ultraviolet radiation in sunlight is broadly divided into UVA and UVB. According to the World Health Organization, WHO, UVA penetrates into the deep dermal layer of the skin, affects connective tissue and blood vessels, reduces skin elasticity, and accelerates photoaging, including wrinkles and sagging. UVB is mostly absorbed by the skin’s surface and causes sunburn, while also damaging DNA and contributing to the development of skin cancer. UVA is also known to increase the risk of skin cancer, and excessive ultraviolet exposure can cause melanoma, squamous cell carcinoma and basal cell carcinoma.
Research has also found that consistently using sunscreen reduces skin aging. In a study published in the international journal Annals of Internal Medicine, 903 adults younger than 55 were observed for approximately 4.5 years. The group that used sunscreen every day showed 24% less progression of skin aging than the group that used it only when necessary.

 ◇Cloudy days are no exception, and a high SPF number is not enough
 Sun protection is necessary even on cloudy days. According to the American Academy of Dermatology, AAD, up to 80% of the sun’s ultraviolet radiation can pass through clouds, so sunscreen should be applied consistently to exposed areas even when the weather is cloudy if outdoor activities are planned.
When choosing a product, check both the SPF number and the broad-spectrum protection label. SPF primarily indicates the level of protection against UVB, which mainly causes sunburn, while broad-spectrum protection indicates whether the product protects against UVA. The AAD recommends a water-resistant product with an SPF of 30 or higher that blocks both UVA and UVB.
How sunscreen is applied is also important. The U.S. Food and Drug Administration, FDA, recommends applying a sufficient amount of sunscreen about 15 minutes before going outdoors and reapplying it at least every 2 hours while outside. It should be reapplied more frequently after swimming or heavy sweating. Areas that are easy to miss, including the ears, nose, back of the neck, backs of the hands, tops of the feet and hairline, should not be overlooked.
 ◇Do not stay in the sun for long just because you are wearing sunscreen
 Applying sunscreen does not mean other sun-protection methods can be skipped. Even when sunscreen is applied, it does not block 100% of ultraviolet radiation, and its effectiveness can decrease because of sweat, water or friction with clothing. The WHO recommends using shade and wearing long-sleeved clothing, a wide-brimmed hat and sunglasses when the ultraviolet index is 3 or higher. Extra care is needed in places that reflect light, such as water, sand and snow, because ultraviolet exposure increases there.
In such situations, sunscreen should be reapplied every 2 hours, and a hat and long sleeves should also be used if the schedule involves prolonged exposure to sunlight.
